title: Ali Nazik
subtitle: Smoked aubergine yoghurt with spiced lamb
excerpt: Charred aubergine blended into garlicky yoghurt, topped with buttery spiced minced lamb. A dish from south-east Turkey that earns its place at any table.
sourceNotes: South-east Turkish kebab tradition, Gaziantep region. Synthesised from multiple Turkish culinary sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The aubergine base can be made a day ahead and refrigerated. Add the lamb topping just before serving.

content.text: Ali nazik is a two-part dish: smoky aubergine stirred into yoghurt, then crowned with spiced minced lamb. The smoke from the aubergine is the whole point. Do not skip the charring step or you will lose the flavour that makes this dish special.
Place the aubergines directly over a gas flame or under a very hot grill. Turn them often with tongs.
Char for 15 to 20 minutes until the skin is black and the flesh collapses. The aubergine should feel completely soft when pressed.
Put the charred aubergines in a colander over the sink. Leave for 10 minutes to cool and drain.
Peel off all the burnt skin. Chop the flesh finely. Squeeze out any excess liquid through the sieve.
Mix the aubergine flesh with the yoghurt, garlic, lemon juice, and salt. Taste and adjust seasoning. Spread across a wide, shallow serving dish.
Melt the butter in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the lamb mince and cook, breaking it up, for 8 minutes until browned.
Add the tomato, green pepper, paprika-hot, and paprika-sweet. Cook for 5 more minutes until the tomato softens and the mixture is fragrant. Season with salt.
Spoon the hot lamb over the aubergine yoghurt. Scatter with sumac and parsley. Serve straight away with flatbread on the side.

items.symptom: The aubergine has no smoky flavour.
items.cause: It was not charred long enough, or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Return it to the flame. The skin must be completely black and cracked before you peel it.

items.cause: The aubergine flesh was not drained well enough.
items.fix: Squeeze the chopped flesh through a sieve or muslin to remove the liquid before mixing.

items.symptom: The lamb is dry and crumbly.
items.cause: It was cooked on too high a heat for too long.
items.fix: Use butter rather than oil and keep the heat at medium. Stop cooking once the liquid has reduced.
